briefs.title: When a stock runs empty
briefs.hook: A toy stock loses more than it gains. Can repeated subtraction make the stock negative?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Distinguish depleted stock from an unmet request when a fixed-flow calculation reaches its zero boundary.

briefs.misconception: A fixed outflow can keep reducing a physical stock below zero.
briefs.objective: Distinguish depleted stock from an unmet request when a fixed-flow calculation reaches its zero boundary.

recall.question: A toy stock starts at 5, gains 1 and is asked to release 4 per round for three rounds. Physical stock remaining?
recall.why: The rule max(0, stock + 1 − 4) reaches zero and stays there; unmet requests are not negative physical stock.

nearest.distinctness: The zero-stock floor becomes active; decide whether a request can be satisfied after physical stock is exhausted, not whether net flow accumulates.
